instructions.en:
1. Sit at the end of a flat bench with a dumbbell resting vertically on each thigh, then lie back while using your knees to help bring the dumbbells up to chest height.
2. Plant your feet firmly on the floor, retract your shoulder blades against the bench, and keep a slight natural arch in your lower back.
3. Press the dumbbells up until your arms are extended, wrists stacked over your elbows, rotating them slightly inward so your elbows don't flare out.
4. Lower the dumbbells under control toward the sides of your chest, elbows at roughly 45-60 degrees from your torso, until you feel a stretch.
5. Press the dumbbells back up in a slight arc without locking out your elbows or letting them touch at the top, exhaling as you press.

instructions.en:
1. Lie back on an incline bench and grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width.
2. Lower the bar slowly and under control to your upper chest.
3. Press the bar back up to full arm extension.

A slow, controlled tempo (for example, a 4-second lowering phase) emphasises time under tension.

instructions.en:
1. Set the bench to a 30-45 degree incline and sit down with a dumbbell resting on each thigh.
2. Lean back against the bench, using your knees to help push the dumbbells up to shoulder height.
3. Plant your feet firmly on the floor and retract your shoulder blades into the bench to stabilise your upper body.
4. Lower the dumbbells slowly toward the upper part of your chest, keeping your elbows at roughly 45-60 degrees from your torso rather than flared out to the sides.
5. Press the dumbbells back up and slightly inward as you exhale, stopping just short of locking out your elbows to keep tension on the upper chest.

instructions.en:
1. Stand holding a barbell with an overhand grip, hands about shoulder-width apart, arms extended in front of your thighs.
2. Keeping the bar close to your body, pull it straight up toward your chin by lifting your elbows out and up.
3. Pause briefly when your elbows reach shoulder height, then lower the bar back down under control.
4. Keep your torso upright throughout; the lift comes from your shoulders and arms, not from swinging your hips.

instructions.en:
1. Sit on the end of a bench with your feet wide apart, holding a dumbbell in one hand.
2. Lean forward and brace the back of your working upper arm against the inside of your thigh, letting the arm hang straight down.
3. Curl the dumbbell up toward your shoulder by bending your elbow, keeping your upper arm pinned against your thigh throughout.
4. Squeeze at the top, then lower the dumbbell under control back to a full stretch.
5. Complete all repetitions, then switch arms.

instructions.en:
1. Hold a dumbbell in each hand and hinge forward at the hips until your torso is close to parallel with the floor, keeping your back flat.
2. Raise your upper arms so they're parallel to the floor and tucked close to your sides, with your elbows bent roughly 90 degrees and forearms hanging down. This is the starting position.
3. Without moving your upper arms, extend your elbows to straighten your arms, squeezing your triceps at the top.
4. Pause briefly, then bend your elbows to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position under control.

1. Lie on your side with your legs stacked and extended, then prop yourself up on your forearm, with your elbow positioned directly under your shoulder.
2. Lift your hips off the floor so your body forms a straight line from your ankles to your shoulders, supporting your weight on your forearm and the side of your lower foot.
3. Keep your hips lifted and your core braced, holding the position without letting your hips sag.
4. Lower back down under control, then repeat on the other side.

instructions.en:
1. Rest a barbell across the front of your shoulders, gripping it with a clean grip (fingertips under the bar, elbows high) or with crossed arms, keeping your elbows up throughout.
2. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, brace your core, and keep your torso upright.
3. Squat down by bending your hips and knees together, keeping your elbows high and chest up so the bar stays balanced on your shoulders.
4. Lower until your hip crease drops below your knees, then drive back up through your feet to standing.

The upright torso this position demands shifts more of the work onto the quadriceps than a back squat.

1. Stand upright holding a dumbbell in each hand, arms at your sides.
2. Step forward with one leg and lower your hips until both knees are bent at about 90 degrees, with the back knee hovering just above the floor.
3. Push through the front heel to return to the starting position.
4. Repeat, alternating legs.

instructions.en:
1. Stand a couple of feet in front of a bench, facing away from it, and rest the top of one foot on the bench behind you.
2. Adjust your front foot forward or back until your stance feels balanced, keeping most of your weight on the front leg.
3. Lower your hips straight down by bending the front knee until your front thigh is roughly parallel to the floor, letting the back knee bend naturally.
4. Keep your torso upright and your front knee tracking over your front foot.
5. Drive through your front heel to return to the starting position. Complete all repetitions, then switch legs.

instructions.en:
1. Kneel on a glute-ham developer (or have a partner brace your ankles) with your hips just in front of the pad and your body upright.
2. Keeping your hips extended and your body in a straight line, slowly lower your torso toward the floor by letting your knees bend.
3. Once you feel a strong stretch through your hamstrings, reverse the movement by contracting your hamstrings and glutes to pull yourself back up to the starting position.
4. Keep the motion slow and controlled in both directions rather than letting gravity do the work.
